Investigate /home/nick/work/llama.cpp (a recent llama.cpp checkout) to determine everything required to build and run a MINIMAL llama.cpp text-generation inference on a BARE-METAL RISC-V (rv64gcv) newlib target: no OS, no Linux, single hart, no pthreads available in libc (newlib), file I/O available through newlib syscalls (open/read/lseek/close via a board runtime), heap via sbrk. Search breadth: very thorough. Report with file:line evidence for every claim.

Answer these specific questions:

a) THREADING: Does the CPU backend reference pthread symbols unconditionally? Look at ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c (ggml_threadpool, ggml_graph_compute), ggml/src/ggml-threading.cpp, ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.cpp. Which pthread functions are called AT RUNTIME when n_threads==1 (mutex/cond init in threadpool creation? barrier? atomic fallbacks?)? Is there any compile-time option to build without threads (search for GGML_OPENMP, _WIN32 thread abstraction, C11 threads fallback)? What is the minimal set of pthread stub functions needed to LINK, and which must actually work for n_threads=1? Also check std::thread usage in libllama core (src/*.cpp) — e.g. llama-model-loader, server only? — and ggml_barrier implementation.

b) MMAP: confirm the no-mmap load path. Look at src/llama-mmap.cpp / src/llama-mmap.h — is mmap compile-time gated on _POSIX_MAPPED_FILES or _WIN32? What does llama_file use (fopen/fread/fseek/ftell or open/pread)? Any posix_fadvise/madvise calls that must exist? What does use_mmap=false do in src/llama-model-loader.cpp (malloc + file read into buffer?).

c) OS/SYSCALL SURFACE: list libc/OS functions the CORE inference path (load model + llama_decode + sampling) would call that turn into newlib syscalls or OS features: clock_gettime/gettimeofday (ggml_time_us in ggml/src/ggml.c — which clock?), sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)?, sched_yield (in spin loops? ggml-cpu), getenv, aligned_alloc/posix_memalign, fstat/ftell for file size, abort/exit. Note anything exotic (eventfd, futex, numa).

d) C++ RUNTIME FEATURES: does core libllama (src/*.cpp) use C++ exceptions (throw/try)? std::filesystem? std::regex? std::thread/std::mutex/std::condition_variable (which files)? Which of these are in core src/ vs common/ vs examples? Is there a minimal example that does NOT link common (check examples/simple/simple.cpp — does it include common.h?)? Could a ~100-line driver against include/llama.h alone do: load model, tokenize, decode loop, sample greedily (llama_sampler chain API is in core?). Also check static initializers / global ctors that matter.

e) RISC-V VECTOR: locate the RVV kernels (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/*, search for __riscv_v_intrinsic, vle32, vlseg). Which ops are vectorized (quants.c dot products? which quant types: q4_0, q8_0, q4_k?)? What cmake flags enable them (GGML_RVV? GGML_RV_ZFH? GGML_CPU_ARCH_FLAGS? RISCV_VECT?)? Is there RUNTIME cpu-feature detection on riscv (getauxval AT_HWCAP? /proc/cpuinfo? ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.cpp cpu feature section) that would break on bare-metal, or is it compile-time? Do any riscv kernels use segment load/store intrinsics (vlseg2e/vsseg — search "seg" in the riscv arch dir)? What VLEN assumptions exist (vsetvl usage / __riscv_vlenb)?

f) MINIMAL BUILD: what cmake configuration would build ONLY libllama + ggml CPU backend as static libs for a Generic (no-OS) system: relevant options (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS, LLAMA_BUILD_TESTS/EXAMPLES/SERVER/TOOLS, LLAMA_CURL, GGML_BACKEND_DL, GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS, GGML_NATIVE). Check ggml/CMakeLists.txt + ggml/src/CMakeLists.txt + ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt for platform assumptions (checks for pthread, dl, rt libs) that fail with CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Generic, and top-level CMakeLists.txt for hard requirements (curl default? git?). Note where -pthread gets added unconditionally.

g) MEMORY FOOTPRINT: from src/llama-context.cpp / llama-kv-cache defaults, note default n_ctx and rough formula for KV+compute buffer memory; just enough to size RAM for a tiny model (e.g. a ~20-50MB GGUF). Nothing precise needed — one paragraph.

Return a structured report, sections a-g, each claim with file:line. This report is the ONLY thing returned to the caller — make it self-contained, no "see above".
